parts.partTitle: Why Git Uses Snapshots & 4 Areas (Not Deltas)

beats.headline: Stop naming folders project-final-v2.
beats.subline: Git isn't cryptic once you see its snapshot model and 4-area map.
beats.narration: If your desktop has project-final-actually-final folders, you need Git. Memorizing commands feels cryptic, until you see the dead-simple snapshot model underneath it.

beats.title: File Deltas vs. Git Snapshots

top.label: Older VCS (SVN)
points: Replays 50 patches just to build v50

bottom.label: Git
points: Every commit snapshots the entire project
Instant branch switching & full offline history

beats.narration: Older tools like Subversion store incremental file diffs. Git takes a full project snapshot on every commit, and simply links to unchanged files instead of copying them. That's why branching and history stay blazing fast.

beats.title: The Four Areas of Git
beats.subtitle: Every Git command moves changes between these 4 zones

nodes.label: Working Directory
nodes.detail: Files you edit in your IDE — not in Git history yet

nodes.label: Staging Area (Index)
nodes.detail: Prep list in .git/index — split bugfixes from typos cleanly

nodes.label: Local Repository (.git)
nodes.detail: Full offline history of commits, branches & tags

nodes.label: Remote Repository
nodes.detail: Shared team server on GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket

beats.narration: Almost every Git command moves code across four areas: your Working Directory on disk, the Staging Area where you pick exact files for a clean commit, your Local Repo in dot git offline, and your Remote Repo on GitHub.

beats.title: Inside .git/objects: Blobs, Trees & Commits
beats.code:
# 3 core objects inside .git/objects:
# Blob   -> compressed file content (40-char SHA-1)
# Tree   -> folder listing (filenames -> blobs/trees)
tree   92b8b694fc1102c64b22cbb24250325492d24263
parent 12a14e9f3ebc7512d506d8705a2e6f49e4198124
author Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>

feat: add customer balance calculation service

steps.explanation: Blobs store deduplicated file content by SHA-1 hash; Trees map filenames and permissions.
Hash includes tree + parent hash—editing old history always creates brand-new commit objects.

beats.narration: Peek inside dot git objects and you'll find three building blocks: Blobs hold compressed content, Trees map filenames, and Commits link a root tree to its parent hash. Change any older commit, and every hash after it changes.

beats.title: Part 1 Locked In
takeaways: Git stores deduplicated snapshots, not file diffs
4 areas: Working Dir → Staging → Local → Remote
Staging splits unrelated edits into focused commits

parts.partTitle: Daily Git Workflow, fetch vs. pull & Java Habits

beats.headline: Stop running git add . blindly.
beats.subline: Master the 6 commands you'll use every single day—plus Java repo hygiene.
beats.narration: Blindly running git add dot and pushing vague messages like 'fix' wrecks team history. Here's the clean daily workflow senior Java devs rely on.

beats.title: The Daily Local Loop
beats.caption: Configure identity once, then check → stage → commit

lines.text: # One-time setup: name, email & default main branch
git commit -m "fix: guard null address in OrderService"

beats.narration: Start with git config for your name, email, and default main branch. Before committing, run git status and git diff to inspect changes. Stage specific files, write a Conventional Commit like fix or feat, and visualize history with git log.

beats.title: git fetch vs. git pull

bottom.label: git pull
bottom.code: git pull  # = git fetch + git merge
points: Immediately merges into your current branch
Use git push -u origin main on first push

beats.narration: Know the difference between fetch and pull. Git fetch safely downloads remote commits without touching your working files, so you can inspect them first. Git pull runs fetch and immediately merges into your current branch.

beats.title: Java .gitignore & Clean Commits
beats.code:
# Compiled bytecode & build outputs
*.class
*.jar
target/
build/
out/
# IDE & OS metadata
.idea/
.vscode/
.DS_Store

steps.explanation: Never commit .class, .jar, target/, or build/—they bloat history and trigger constant conflicts.
Ignore .idea/, .vscode/, and .DS_Store so teammates on Mac, Linux, and Windows never clash.

beats.narration: In every Java repo, add a dot gitignore on day one. Keep compiled dot class files, jars, target and build folders, plus dot idea and dot vscode out of Git so you never bloat history or clash across laptops.

beats.title: Daily Workflow Mastered
takeaways: git fetch previews safely; git pull fetches & merges

parts.partTitle: Branching, Merge vs. Rebase, Conflicts & git reflog

beats.headline: A Git branch is just 41 bytes.
beats.subline: Zero file copying—just a tiny pointer. Here's how to branch, merge, and recover safely.
beats.narration: Creating a Git branch doesn't copy your project—it's literally a 41-byte file holding one commit hash, while HEAD tracks where you are right now.

beats.title: git merge vs. git rebase

top.label: git merge (Safe for Shared)
top.code:
git switch main
git merge feature/discount-rules
points: Fast-forward if main didn't move; else 3-way merge commit
Safe for shared branches & Pull Requests

bottom.label: git rebase (Private Branches Only!)
bottom.code:
git switch -c feature/login
git rebase main
points: Replays commits linearly with brand-new hashes
NEVER rebase commits already pushed to teammates!

beats.narration: Use git switch dash c to branch. Merging fast-forwards if main hasn't moved, or creates a three-way merge commit without changing hashes. Rebase replays commits linearly with brand-new hashes—great on private branches, but never rebase commits you already pushed to teammates.

beats.title: Resolving Merge Conflicts Cleanly

steps.explanation: Your current branch's version—everything between <<<<<<< HEAD and =======.
Incoming branch's version. Keep one or combine both, delete all 3 markers, compile & test, then git add + commit!

beats.narration: When two branches edit the same lines, Git inserts conflict markers: top is HEAD, bottom is incoming. Keep what you need, delete all three markers, compile and test, then git add and commit—or bail with git merge dash dash abort.

beats.title: Rescuing Lost Commits with git reflog
beats.caption: Accidental git reset --hard? Committed snapshots survive ~30 days!

lines.text: git reset --hard HEAD~2   # Oops! Commits vanished?
# Restore into a new branch (also saves Detached HEAD!)

beats.narration: Accidentally ran git reset dash dash hard? Don't panic. Git keeps committed snapshots in dot git objects for around thirty days. Run git reflog to find the old hash, then run git switch dash c to rescue it into a fresh branch.

beats.title: Chapter Complete! Try the Lab
takeaways: Branch = 41-byte pointer; never rebase shared commits
Conflicts: edit, remove markers, test, add & commit
git reflog rescues committed work (commit small & often!)
beats.narration: You've got the full Git mental model—from snapshots to reflog rescues. Checkout the companion branch in java hub resources to practice the hands-on lab yourself.
